summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, and hypertension was admitted for nausea, vomiting, fever, and coffee-ground emesis. He was found to have influenza, which explained his fevers and gastrointestinal symptoms. An upper GI bleed was suspected due to the emesis, but endoscopy was deferred due to a vagal episode causing hypotension. His hemoglobin dropped but stabilized without transfusion. A new diagnosis of systolic heart failure was made after an echocardiogram showed reduced ejection fraction, prompting cardiology consultation and medication adjustments. Possible Chagas cardiomyopathy was identified via serology, with recommendations sent to primary care. Pleural effusions and wheezing were managed with diuresis and albuterol. He completed a dialysis session during admission for hyperkalemia and was discharged stable on day four with follow-up plans for cardiology and pulmonary function testing.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
